paragraph: Hearing Rama grant permission to Sita, Lakshmana fell at his brother's feet and begged to let him also accompany them. Lakshmana looked pleadingly at Sita and then at Rama who was reputed never to abandon any, who sought refuge in him, 'Even if there is a place on this earth where there is neither old age nor death, I do not desire it. Without you, I do not want kingship heaven or earth". Rama said, "Lakshmana, you are not only my brother but my friend and my life. What of Kausalya and Sumitra if you go with me? The king enticed by Kaikeyi may slight them and she with the kingdom in her hands, may not do them justice. Indebted to Kaikeyi trying to please her, Bharata may not spare much thought to my mothers. Stay back Lakshmana, there is no greater dharma than serving one's parents." Lakshmana who refused to be dissuaded said, "Kausalya can take charge of a thousand Lakshmanas like me and bear them. So can Sumitra who is equally competent. As for Bharata, he is a noble Ikshvaku and will cherish the queens with the greatest of love and reverence. Take me with you, I will be your servant." Moved by Lakshmana's devotion, Rama agreed saying, "Go bid farewell to those dear to you. Bring with you the bows and the quivers, the swords and armor". Darting away happily, he also brought back Suyajna son of Vasishta and his disciples into Rama's presence along with other eminent Brahmins so that they could pay them their worshipful homage before departing.
Situation/Problem_Faced: Lakshmana desperately seeks to accompany Rama into exile, creating a conflict between fraternal devotion and filial duty, as Rama worries about their mothers' welfare in their absence.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Lakshmana demonstrates absolute devotion to Rama while rationally addressing his concerns about their mothers. Rama ultimately accepts Lakshmana's companionship after being moved by his sincerity.
Outcome/Resolution: Rama grants Lakshmana permission to join the exile, leading to joyful preparation for their departure while ensuring proper spiritual ceremonies are observed.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.stress Management: Worry alleviation, Protective reasoning, Concern mitigation

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Bandhutva (Sacred Brotherhood - Lakshmana embodies the ideal of selfless fraternal devotion)
Sharanagati (Absolute Surrender - Lakshmana's complete submission to Rama's will)
Mata-Pitri Bhakti (Mother-Father Devotion - The brothers' debate reflects this core Hindu value)
Sahaja Dharma (Natural Duty - Lakshmana follows his inherent nature of service)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: This episode exemplifies Bandhutva (sacred brotherhood) through Lakshmana's Sharanagati (total surrender) to Rama, resolving the tension between Mata-Pitri Bhakti (parental devotion) and Sahaja Dharma (innate duty). The spiritual preparation (bringing Brahmins for homage) underscores the journey's sacred nature.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Psychologically, this shows healthy attachment functioning - Lakshmana's separation anxiety is validated and resolved through Rama's compassionate acceptance. Their ability to rationally address concerns while honoring emotional needs demonstrates mature relationship dynamics and effective coping strategies.
